name: Gregg Hymowitz
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Gregg S. Hymowitz is chairman and CEO of EnTrust Global, an alternative asset management firm with $15.2B in assets under management.
He founded the firm in 1997, sold a majority stake to Legg Mason in 2016 and repurchased the entire interest from Franklin Templeton in 2020.
Hymowitz joined Goldman, Sachs & Co. In 1992 and became a vice president at the firm before leaving in 1997.
He graduated cum laude from Harvard Law School in 1990, and received a BA, Phi Beta Kappa, from the State University of New York at Binghamton in 1987.
Hymowitz most recently sold an additional minority stake in EnTrust to the Brunei Sovereign Wealth Fund, which now owns 20%.
forbes_facts: Hymowitz endowed the Hymowitz Family Professorship of the Practice Fund (Duke Global Health Institute).
Hymowitz is a former board member of the Board of Trustees of Montefiore Medical Center and served two terms as a Trustee of the Riverdale Country Day School.

name: Ronald Clarke
sec_insider_companies: CORPAY, INC. (CPAY) - CEO & Chairman of BOD; Dayforce, Inc. (DAY) - Director
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Ronald Clarke is the CEO and chairman of Corpay, a $3.9 billion (sales) digital payments company.
The Atlanta-based company offers businesses credit cards geared to travel expenses like gas, tolls and lodging.
Clarke joined the company in 2000. Ten years later, he took it public on the New York Stock Exchange under its previous name, FleetCor.
Corpay has some 800,000 customers and operates in more than 100 countries worldwide.

name: Amnon Shashua
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Amnon Shashua is the cofounder and CEO of autonomous vehicle technology firm Mobileye.
A computer science professor at Hebrew University, Shashua launched the company in 1999 with fellow billionaire Ziv Aviram.
The pair took Mobileye public in 2014, then sold it to Intel in 2017 at a $15.3 billion valuation.
Aviram and Shashua also co-CEOs of Or-Cam, which makes portable, artificial vision devices for visually impaired people. They founded it in 2010.

name: Tony Xu
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2021-2023); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2020)
forbes_bio: Tony Xu cofounded restaurant delivery service DoorDash in 2013 and became a billionaire after its 2020 IPO. He owns 4.6% plus options.
Cofounders Andy Fang and Stanley Tang, who Xu met while they were all studying at Stanford, own about 4% each. Xu is the CEO.
DoorDash is America's largest food delivery service. It delivers meals and more from 390,000 restaurants and other merchants like CVS.
Xu was born in China and moved to the U.S. at age five. Growing up, his mom worked as a server at a Chinese restaurant.

name: Seth Klarman
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Seth Klarman runs Boston-based hedge fund Baupost, which has $27.4 billion under management as of March 2023.
Klarman's book "Margin of Safety," a cult classic among value investors, sells for about $1,700 on Amazon.
Once a major donor to the Republican Party, Klarman publicly denounced Trump in 2016, and has been contributing to the Democratic Party.
forbes_facts: In 2017, Klarman's horse, Cloud Computing, won the Preakness Stakes at Pimlico, the racetrack he grew up next to in Baltimore.
Klarman, whose philanthropic efforts focus on scientific research and promoting access to music learning, is also a major supporter of causes in Israel.

name: Rahul Dhoot
forbes_bio: Rahul Dhoot founded and runs Aurangabad-based auto components maker Dhoot Tranmission, which manufactures wiring harnesses for two-and-three-wheelers.
It also makes electronics, sensors, EV systems and automotive switches.
The company has operations in India, the U.K., Slovakia, Thailand, South Korea and Japan.
Dhoot has an undergrad degree in electronics and telecoms engineering.
The company got listed in August 2026 in an IPO that was oversubscribed 74 times.

name: Christopher Stolte
forbes_bio: Christopher Stolte cofounded data analytics company Tableau in 2003.
Salesforce acquired Tableau in June 2019 in a $15.7 billion, all-stock deal.
Stolte left Tableau that year and now runs his family foundation?which focuses on climate, education and civic engagement causes.
Tableau was born out of Stolte's Stanford thesis, analyzing and visualizing databases under his then-advisor, later-cofounder Pat Hanrahan.
He and his cofounders raised just $15 million in venture capital before taking Tableau public in May 2013.

name: Zhao Jianhui
forbes_bio: Zhao jianhui is the chairman of Epiworld International, a maker of silicon carbide (SiC) epitaxial wafers used in power devices for sectors such as EV, renewable energy and AI.
It is the world's largest SiC epitaxial foundry by both revenue and sales volume, accounting for roughly a third of the global market in 2024.
Zhang founded the company in 2011 and took it public on the Hong Kong stock exchange in March 2026.
Zhang has over 35 years of research experience and is the first IEEE Fellow selected based on their contributions to SiC technologies.
He serves as chair professor at Xiamen University in China and worked with Rutgers University in the U.S.
